content: _Acinetobacter_ is a group of bacteria commonly found in the environment, such as in soil and water. Infections caused by these bacteria are rare outside of healthcare settings but can be serious when they occur. The most common type of _Acinetobacter_ that causes infections in humans belongs to the _Acinetobacter baumannii_ family, often referred to as the _Acinetobacter baumannii complex_. Infections caused by _Acinetobacter baumannii_ can affect various parts of the body, including the bloodstream, urinary tract, lungs (causing pneumonia), or wounds. In some cases, individuals may carry the bacteria without showing signs of infection, a condition known as colonization. Certain populations are at higher risk of _Acinetobacter_ infections, particularly patients in healthcare settings. Those most vulnerable include individuals on ventilators, those with medical devices such as catheters, patients with open surgical wounds, individuals in intensive care units, and those with prolonged hospital stays. Additionally, people with weakened immune systems, chronic lung disease, or diabetes are more susceptible to these infections. The bacteria can spread in healthcare environments through contact with contaminated surfaces, medical equipment, or person-to-person transmission, often via the hands of healthcare workers. To reduce the risk of infection, patients and caregivers should practice good hand hygiene by washing hands with soap and water or using alcohol-based hand sanitizers, especially before and after caring for wounds or handling medical devices. Patients should also remind healthcare providers to clean their hands before touching them or their medical equipment. In healthcare settings, it is essential to allow staff to clean patient rooms daily and to follow strict infection control practices. To diagnose an _Acinetobacter_ infection, healthcare providers collect a specimen from the patient and send it to a laboratory for antimicrobial susceptibility testing. This testing identifies the most effective antibiotic for treating the infection. Treatment typically involves antibiotics, but many _Acinetobacter_ strains are resistant to multiple antibiotics, making them challenging to treat. The choice of antibiotic depends on the test results, as well as other factors such as potential side effects and interactions with other medications. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is actively working to combat _Acinetobacter_ infections. Their efforts include providing testing to identify cases of antimicrobial resistance, tracking infections through programs like the Emerging Infections Program, and sharing data on the AR & Patient Safety Portal. The CDC collaborates with health departments, federal agencies, healthcare providers, and patients to prevent _Acinetobacter_ infections and slow the spread of antibiotic-resistant strains.
